name: Finasteride
route_note: Oral tablet once daily (5 mg for BPH, 1 mg for hair loss); topical spray approved in some countries

discovery.by: Merck Research Laboratories (team including Gary Rasmusson)
discovery.note: Inspired by Julianne Imperato-McGinley's 1974 study of men with inherited 5α-reductase deficiency, who had small prostates and no male-pattern baldness.

tagline: 5α-reductase inhibitor for prostate enlargement and male-pattern hair loss
summary: Finasteride inhibits the enzyme that converts testosterone to the more potent androgen dihydrotestosterone (DHT). It shrinks the enlarged prostate in benign prostatic hyperplasia and slows male-pattern hair loss, and has been the subject of safety debates about persistent sexual and psychiatric effects.
mechanism: Finasteride is a competitive, mechanism-based inhibitor of type II 5α-reductase (and type III), forming a stable complex with the enzyme and reducing serum DHT by about 70%.
Lower DHT shrinks prostate tissue over months, improving urinary symptoms and reducing the risk of urinary retention and surgery. In the scalp, lower DHT slows follicle miniaturisation.
uses: Symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia (alone or with an alpha blocker)

history.title: Inspiration
history.detail: Imperato-McGinley describes men in the Dominican Republic with 5α-reductase deficiency.

history.title: BPH approval
history.detail: FDA approves Proscar for benign prostatic hyperplasia.

history.title: Hair loss
history.detail: FDA approves Propecia 1 mg for male-pattern hair loss.

history.title: Prostate Cancer Prevention Trial
history.detail: PCPT shows a 25% reduction in prostate cancer prevalence but more high-grade tumours.

history.title: High-grade cancer warning
history.detail: FDA adds a warning about increased risk of high-grade prostate cancer to 5α-reductase inhibitor labels.

history.title: Persistent sexual effects
history.detail: FDA updates labels to note sexual adverse effects that may continue after stopping.

history.title: Suicidality
history.detail: FDA adds suicidal ideation and behaviour to the Propecia label.

history.title: EU review
history.detail: EMA's safety committee confirms suicidal ideation as a side effect of oral and topical finasteride.

facts: Finasteride lowers PSA by about half, so PSA values are adjusted during treatment.
Women who are or may become pregnant should not handle crushed or broken tablets because of the risk to a male fetus.
